Split System A/C.description: Most common residential cooling system. Indoor evaporator + outdoor condensing unit connected by line set.
commonConfigurations: 1.5 to 5 ton capacity
R-410A or R-22 (older units)
Fixed orifice (piston) or TXV metering
PSC or ECM blower motor indoor
Single-stage or two-stage compressor
topFailures: Bad capacitor (run cap)
Low refrigerant charge
Dirty condenser coil
Dirty filter causing coil freeze
Contactor failure

seasonalIssues.spring: First startup after winter: check capacitors, contactor, refrigerant charge. Clean condenser coil. Cottonwood season clogs coils.
seasonalIssues.summer: Peak load failures: capacitors fail in heat, compressors overheat, high head pressure from dirty condensers.
seasonalIssues.fall: End of season: check for leaks before shutdown. Service reversing valve if heat pump.
seasonalIssues.winter: Heat pump defrost issues. Frozen outdoor coil. Auxiliary heat not engaging.

criticalMeasurements.suctionLineTemp: Should feel cold, slight condensation, NOT frosted
criticalMeasurements.liquidLineTemp: Should feel warm (90-110°F), NOT hot to touch

Heat Pump.description: Reversible system providing both heating and cooling. Uses reversing valve to switch between modes.
commonConfigurations: 2-5 ton capacity
R-410A primary
TXV metering (most modern units)
Two metering devices (one for each mode) or bi-directional TXV
Defrost cycle: reverse cycle or demand defrost
topFailures: Stuck reversing valve
Defrost board failure
Outdoor coil icing up
Auxiliary heat not working
Low charge in heat mode

heatModeCharging.notes: Charging in heat mode is different - use manufacturer's heat mode charging chart
heatModeCharging.superheatTarget: Measured at outdoor coil in heat mode: 5-10°F
heatModeCharging.subcoolingTarget: Measured at indoor coil in heat mode: varies by manufacturer
heatModeCharging.caution: Do NOT charge to standard cooling mode targets when in heat mode

defrostDiagnostics.normalDefrost: System should defrost every 30-90 minutes in cold weather. Defrost cycle: reversing valve switches to cool, outdoor fan stops, heat strips energize. Cycle lasts 2-10 minutes.
defrostDiagnostics.failedDefrost: Outdoor coil fully iced over. Check defrost thermostat (should close at ~32°F), defrost board timer, outdoor coil sensor.
defrostDiagnostics.frequentDefrost: Low charge, airflow restriction, or defrost control set too aggressively. Check charge and outdoor coil condition.

Mini-Split.description: Ductless system with wall-mounted indoor head(s) connected to outdoor unit. Inverter-driven variable speed compressor.
commonConfigurations: 9K-36K BTU single zone
Multi-zone: 2-5 indoor heads on one outdoor
R-410A or R-32
All use EEV metering
DC inverter compressor (variable speed)
topFailures: Communication error (indoor/outdoor)
Inverter board failure
EEV stepper motor
Drain pump failure
Indoor PCB fault
diagnosticDifferences: Error codes displayed on indoor unit or remote - always check first
Inverter compressors ramp up/down - amp draw varies, can't compare to fixed RLA
EEV controlled by PCB - no manual adjustment possible
Line set lengths critical - check manufacturer max distance and height differential
Communication wiring: polarity-sensitive on most brands. Wrong polarity = comm error.
Most mini-splits need specific vacuum and charge procedures - follow OEM manual
Mini-Split.chargingNotes: Most mini-splits come pre-charged for 25ft line set. Add refrigerant per manufacturer's spec for additional line set length. ALWAYS weigh in charge - never charge by pressures alone on inverter systems.

RTU (Rooftop).description: Self-contained package unit installed on commercial building roof. Contains all components in one cabinet.
commonConfigurations: 3-25 ton commercial
R-410A or R-407C
Multiple compressor circuits
Economizer with enthalpy or dry-bulb control
BAS/DDC integration
topFailures: Economizer damper failure (stuck open = excess humidity)
Belt drive blower issues
Multiple compressor staging problems
Roof leak at curb penetration
Enthalpy sensor failure

economizer.purpose: Uses outdoor air for free cooling when outdoor conditions allow
economizer.diagnostics: Check damper actuator, enthalpy sensor, minimum position setting. Stuck open economizer = high humidity complaints. Stuck closed = no free cooling benefit.
economizer.settings: Changeover typically at 65-70°F dry bulb or 28 BTU/lb enthalpy

Package Unit.description: All components in single outdoor cabinet. No indoor unit - supply and return ducts connect directly.
topFailures: Same as split system PLUS: duct connection leaks, cabinet water intrusion, pest/rodent damage to wiring
specialNotes: All electrical connections exposed to weather - check for corrosion
Supply air ductwork directly exposed - check for condensation and mold
Filter access often on exterior - customers forget to change
Gas heat section (if equipped) subject to wind interference - check flame pattern

Gas Furnace.description: Forced-air heating appliance burning natural gas or propane. Heat transferred to supply air via heat exchanger. 80% AFUE (single heat exchanger, atmospheric/induced draft) or 90%+ AFUE (secondary heat exchanger, condensing, PVC venting).
uniqueComponents: Hot surface ignitor (HSI) — silicon nitride or silicon carbide
Pressure switch(es) — one per stage on multi-stage units
Gas valve (24VAC, single or two-stage or modulating)
Flue/vent system (Cat I metal for 80%, Cat IV PVC for 90%+)
Condensate trap and drain (90%+ units only)
commonConfigurations: 40,000-120,000 BTU input residential
80% AFUE single-stage (B-vent metal flue)
90-98% AFUE condensing (PVC vent + intake)
Single-stage, two-stage, or modulating gas valve
PSC, X13, or ECM blower motor
Upflow, downflow, horizontal, or multi-position cabinet
Natural gas or LP propane (requires conversion kit)
topFailures: Flame sensor coated with oxidation — won't prove flame, lockout after trial for ignition
Hot surface ignitor cracked (brittle silicon nitride, drops and fractures)
Pressure switch stuck open (blocked vent, condensate trap full, hose collapsed)
Inducer motor bearings failing (loud humming, slow startup, pressure switch fault)
Cracked heat exchanger (CO in supply air, often shows up after 12-15 years)
High limit switch tripping (low airflow, dirty filter, blower issue)
Blocked condensate drain causing pressure switch fault on 90%+ units
Rollout switch tripped (flame rolling out of burner box — DO NOT bypass, find root cause)
Gas valve coil failure (ohm test 24VAC coils: typically 30-80 ohms)

seasonalIssues.spring: End-of-heating-season: pull blower, vacuum burners, inspect heat exchanger with camera/mirror, check flame pattern for orange/yellow tipping. Clean flame sensor with fine emery cloth — NOT sandpaper.
seasonalIssues.summer: Off-season — moisture/rust accumulates in heat exchanger and burners. Spider webs in burner orifices common. AC running through same blower can stress motor bearings.
seasonalIssues.fall: Pre-season tune-up critical: replace HSI if marginal ohms, test all safety switches, verify gas pressure (manifold + inlet), perform combustion analysis, draft test, CO test in flue and supply air.
seasonalIssues.winter: Peak load failures — ignitor failure is the most common no-heat call. Pressure switch issues from snow/ice blocking concentric PVC vents. Frozen condensate line on 90%+ units.

criticalMeasurements.temperatureRise: Must be within nameplate range, typically 35-65°F. Measure in supply 6 ft from furnace and return upstream of any heat source. High rise = low airflow. Low rise = too much airflow or undersized burner.
criticalMeasurements.manifoldGasPressure: Natural gas: 3.5 inches WC (single-stage) or 1.7/3.5 inches WC (two-stage low/high). LP: 10-11 inches WC. Measure with manometer at outlet pressure tap on gas valve.
criticalMeasurements.inletGasPressure: Natural gas: 5-10.5 inches WC static, must not drop below 5 inches WC under load. LP: 11-14 inches WC.
criticalMeasurements.totalExternalStaticPressure: Should not exceed nameplate (typically 0.5-0.8 inches WC). Measure supply (after coil) and return (before filter), add absolute values.
criticalMeasurements.flameSignalMicroamps: 2-6 µA DC healthy. Below 1 µA = clean or replace flame sensor. Most boards lock out below 0.7 µA.
criticalMeasurements.coInSupplyAir: 0 ppm — ANY measurable CO in supply air = cracked heat exchanger, shut down immediately.
criticalMeasurements.coAirFreeFlue: Below 100 ppm air-free acceptable. Above 400 ppm air-free = service required.

heatingSequenceOfOperation: 1. Thermostat calls for heat — W terminal energized, 24VAC
2. IFC board receives W signal, energizes inducer motor immediately
3. Inducer creates negative pressure in vent system (15-30 sec spin-up)
4. Pressure switch closes when sufficient draft proven (typically 0.4-1.5 inches WC vacuum)
5. IFC energizes hot surface ignitor (15-45 sec warmup, glows bright orange/white)
6. Gas valve opens (24VAC to MV terminal), gas flows to burners
8. Flame sensor proves flame within 4-7 second trial-for-ignition (DC microamp signal)
10. Blower delay timer (30-90 sec) then blower energizes on heat speed
11. High limit and rollout limits monitor for overheat throughout cycle
12. Thermostat satisfied: gas valve closes, inducer post-purges 15-30 sec, blower runs off-delay 60-180 sec
diagnosticDifferences: Always check error code/flash code on IFC board first — tells you which stage failed
Most failures present as no heat but root cause varies wildly by sequence stage
Never bypass a safety switch to get it running — safety switches indicate a real problem
Heat exchanger inspection requires camera + CO test + flame disturbance test
Combustion analyzer is mandatory for 90%+ units and best practice for all gas appliances

Air Handler (AHU).description: Indoor blower cabinet used with heat pumps and split systems where no furnace is present. Contains evaporator coil, blower, and optional electric heat strips. Acts as both cooling air mover and primary/auxiliary heat source on heat pump systems.
uniqueComponents: Blower motor (PSC, X13, or ECM/variable speed)
Electric resistance heat strips (5-25 kW typical)
Auxiliary limit switch on heat strips
Condensate drain pan (primary + secondary on attic units)
Float safety switch on secondary pan
Optional humidifier/UV light/MERV filter rack connections
commonConfigurations: 1.5-5 ton residential
Multi-position: upflow, downflow, horizontal left, horizontal right
Heat strip kits: 5, 7.5, 10, 15, 20, 25 kW (sized to backup heat pump capacity at design temp)
ECM motors with multi-speed taps for cooling/heating/continuous fan
TXV (most common) or piston for budget/older units
Cased coil + matched blower section, or all-in-one cabinet
topFailures: ECM motor module failure (electronic module on motor body — replace module separately, not full motor)
Heat strip element burnout (one element opens, reduces capacity but unit still runs on remaining elements)
Heat strip sequencer stuck closed (strips run when not called) or open (no aux heat)
Clogged condensate drain — float switch trips, system shuts down
Frozen evaporator coil from low airflow or low refrigerant charge
TXV sensing bulb lost charge (high superheat, low cooling capacity)
Blower wheel coated with debris (vibration, noise, reduced CFM)
Float switch failure (false trips or fails to trip during actual overflow)

seasonalIssues.spring: Inspect drain pan and primary/secondary drain lines — flush with vinegar, check float switches by lifting float manually, verify drain slope 1/8 inch per foot minimum.
seasonalIssues.summer: Condensate drain failures most common service call. Frozen coils from dirty filters. Attic AHUs run very hot — check for rodent damage to wiring.
seasonalIssues.fall: Test heat strips before heating season — pull amp draw on each element with clamp meter. Verify sequencer staging.
seasonalIssues.winter: Heat strips cycling excessively = heat pump not keeping up. Check balance point setting on thermostat. Aux heat lockout temperature setting.

criticalMeasurements.deltaTHeatStrips: Calculated: Rise (°F) = (kW × 3413) / (1.08 × CFM). Example: 10 kW at 1200 CFM = 26°F rise
criticalMeasurements.heatStripAmpDraw: Each 5 kW element draws approximately 21 amps at 240V. Total amps = sum of all energized elements + blower amps.
criticalMeasurements.totalExternalStaticPressure: 0.5 inches WC nominal residential, do not exceed 0.8 inches WC
criticalMeasurements.supplyAirTempHeatStrips: Typically 95-130°F depending on kW and airflow

diagnosticDifferences: ECM motors do not respond to capacitor testing — they have onboard electronics, test with motor-specific procedures or substitute test motor
Heat strips on heat pump only run as auxiliary/emergency — check thermostat config (balance point, lockout temp) before condemning strips
Multi-stage heat strips stage on sequencer with 15-60 sec delays between stages — verify staging with amp clamp
Float switch in secondary pan opens 24V circuit — no cooling complaint with normal refrigerant pressures often means float tripped
Variable-speed ECM blowers self-adjust to maintain CFM against static — high static hides itself in CFM but shows up as elevated motor amp draw and noise

Geothermal Heat Pump.description: Heat pump that exchanges heat with the earth or groundwater instead of outdoor air. Typically 3-5x more efficient than air-source heat pumps. Loop fluid (water or water/antifreeze mix) circulates between earth loop and refrigerant-to-water heat exchanger inside the unit.
uniqueComponents: Refrigerant-to-water coaxial or brazed-plate heat exchanger (source side)
Refrigerant-to-air heat exchanger or hydronic coil (load side)
Loop circulator pump(s) — flow center with isolation valves
Water flow switch (prevents compressor operation without loop flow)
Loop pressure gauge and purge ports
Desuperheater coil for domestic hot water preheat (optional)
Antifreeze solution — methanol, ethanol, or propylene glycol depending on climate and code
HDPE loop piping (closed loop) or pump-and-dump well assembly (open loop)
commonConfigurations: Closed loop horizontal: 4-6 ft deep trenches, 300-600 ft per ton, most common residential
Closed loop vertical: 150-450 ft deep boreholes, 150-200 ft per ton, limited land area
Pond/lake loop: submerged HDPE pipe coils, requires 8 ft minimum depth and adequate volume
Open loop (pump-and-dump): well water in, discharged to second well or surface, requires excellent water quality
Capacity: 2-6 ton residential, larger for commercial
Refrigerant: R-410A primary, R-32 in newer equipment
topFailures: Loop pressure loss (leak in pipe, fittings, or flow center — may be slow)
Air entrained in loop (causes pump cavitation, reduced flow, noise, compressor trips)
Loop pump (circulator) failure or seized impeller
Fouled coaxial heat exchanger (open loop with mineral deposits or iron bacteria)
Low charge on refrigerant side (same as air-source, just harder to diagnose with water temps)
Antifreeze concentration too low (winter freeze risk) or too high (reduced heat transfer)
Open loop: pump-and-dump well pump failure, biofouling, iron scale
Desuperheater check valve stuck (DHW tank cold or refrigerant migration)

seasonalIssues.spring: Verify loop pressure stable after winter ground contraction. Top off if needed with same antifreeze solution. Inspect flow center for leaks.
seasonalIssues.summer: Load on cooling — entering water temperature climbs as season progresses. Marginal loops show capacity loss in August. Open loop wells: monitor flow rate and water quality.
seasonalIssues.fall: Pre-heating-season check: loop pressure, antifreeze freeze point with refractometer, pump amp draw, entering water temp baseline.
seasonalIssues.winter: Entering water temp can drop to 25-35°F on undersized loops. Compressor low suction trips if loop frozen or flow too low. Antifreeze critical — test freeze point annually.

criticalMeasurements.enteringWaterTemp: Closed loop heating: 25-50°F. Closed loop cooling: 60-90°F. Open loop: typically 50-60°F year-round.
criticalMeasurements.leavingWaterTemp: 5-12°F differential from entering water temp typical
criticalMeasurements.loopFlowRate: 3 GPM per ton minimum, target 3-4 GPM per ton closed loop
criticalMeasurements.loopFreezePoint: 20°F below lowest expected entering water temp — typically -5°F to 15°F depending on climate

diagnosticDifferences: Charging and diagnostics use entering water temp instead of outdoor ambient — manufacturer charts based on water temps
Symptoms of loop problems mimic refrigerant problems — ALWAYS verify loop flow and entering water temp before touching refrigerant
Flow proving required: most units have flow switch or pressure differential sensor that locks out compressor on low flow
Open loop water quality drives reliability — hardness, iron, pH, bacteria all foul heat exchanger. Annual flush often required.
Loop purging: must achieve 2-3 ft per second velocity to flush air — requires high-flow purge cart
Loop pressure tests: 100 psig hold for 30 min on closed loop after install, recheck annually

VRF System (Variable Refrigerant Flow).description: Multi-zone commercial/light-commercial heat pump using refrigerant as the only working fluid distributed to multiple indoor units. Variable-speed inverter compressor modulates capacity 10-100%. Heat recovery (3-pipe) versions can simultaneously heat and cool different zones. Major brands: Mitsubishi City Multi, Daikin VRV, LG Multi V, Samsung, Fujitsu.
uniqueComponents: Inverter scroll compressor(s) — typically 2 in larger units for redundancy
Branch selector boxes / branch controllers (3-pipe heat recovery only)
Multiple electronic expansion valves (one per indoor unit plus system EEVs)
Refrigerant oil separator and oil management system
Multiple solenoid valves for mode switching
Indoor units: ducted, cassette, wall-mount, floor console, ceiling-suspended
commonConfigurations: 2-pipe heat pump (cool OR heat, all zones same mode)
3-pipe heat recovery (simultaneous heat and cool different zones — VRF signature feature)
Outdoor capacity: 6-30 tons single condenser, modular up to 60+ tons
Up to 64 indoor units per outdoor on large systems
Refrigerant piping runs up to 1000 ft total (varies by brand)
R-410A primary, R-32 in newer equipment
Indoor capacity ratio: 50-150% of outdoor allowed
topFailures: Refrigerant leak in long pipe runs — large charges (50-200+ lbs), hardest to find
Communication errors between outdoor, branch boxes, indoor units — wiring polarity and terminations
EEV stepper motor failure on any of dozens of expansion valves in system
Branch selector solenoid valve failure — stuck mode, hot/cold complaints
Inverter board failure (PCB) — very expensive, requires brand-specific replacement
Oil return problems on long vertical risers — undersized lines or missing oil traps
Field commissioning errors — more failures from bad installation than equipment defects

seasonalIssues.spring: Shoulder season heat-recovery testing — verify mode switching as different zones call heating and cooling simultaneously.
seasonalIssues.summer: Peak cooling — oil return critical at full load. Check discharge superheat.
seasonalIssues.fall: Heating season prep — test heating mode in all zones. Defrost cycles begin.
seasonalIssues.winter: Defrost and low-ambient operation. Some VRF systems lose capacity below 0°F unless cold-climate rated (vapor injection technology).

criticalMeasurements.refrigerantCharge: Per manufacturer calculation: base charge + (length × per-foot factor) for each pipe size. Must be weighed in precisely — 5% variance causes performance issues.
criticalMeasurements.subcoolingDischarge: Manufacturer-specific — typically 15-25°F at outdoor unit liquid line
criticalMeasurements.dischargePressureR410A: 350-450 psig depending on conditions and load
criticalMeasurements.dischargeTemp: 180-220°F normal. Above 230°F = compressor protection trip imminent.
criticalMeasurements.communicationVoltage: DC voltage between communication terminals: typically 10-30 VDC pulsing (brand-specific)
criticalMeasurements.pipeSizingVerification: Liquid lines: 3/8 to 1-1/8 inch. Suction/discharge: 1/2 to 1-5/8 inch. Must match design — undersized causes oil return failure.
criticalMeasurements.heightDifferential: Outdoor above indoors: max 110-165 ft typical. Indoor to indoor: max 49 ft typical. Brand-specific limits.

diagnosticDifferences: Always start at the manufacturer's service tool/laptop interface — reveals error history, EEV positions, sensor temps for all units simultaneously
Each manufacturer has proprietary diagnostic software (Mitsubishi MN Converter, Daikin Service Checker, LG LGMV) — you cannot properly service VRF without it
Heat recovery vs heat pump: 3-pipe systems have branch selector boxes between outdoor and indoors. 2-pipe systems do not.
Refrigerant charge calculation must be documented and posted on outdoor unit — service tech needs this for any subsequent work
Pump-down for VRF service: cannot pump down to outdoor unit like split system — must recover to cylinders or use isolation valves at each indoor unit
Commissioning is critical — improper line sizing, missing oil traps, incomplete leak test cause years of chronic issues
A2L refrigerant (R-32) charge-to-room-volume safety calculation required — smallest indoor unit space must be adequate for system charge volume
